_readme: Contracts and owner addresses belonging to identifiable, accountable issuers.
A match subtracts 50 points, because the question this scanner answers is
'how much must you trust someone, and who?' - and a named, regulated issuer
is a very different answer from an anonymous wallet holding the same powers.
1. Only add an address you have personally verified. This list LOWERS risk
scores, so a wrong entry makes something dangerous look safe. That is the
worst failure this tool can have.
2. Record how you verified it in 'verifiedBy'. 'I think it is' is not a source.
3. Prefer contract addresses over owner addresses. Block explorers label
well-known contracts; the wallets that control them usually carry no label
at all, so claiming one belongs to a company is normally a guess.
- Being a known issuer means accountable, not harmless. Circle can and does
freeze USDC. The discount reflects who holds the power, not whether the
power exists - the privileges are still listed in full.
- Matching on owner cannot see role-based control. A contract can name a
reputable owner while a separate role holder retains the dangerous powers.
- Addresses differ per chain. An entry is scoped to the chain it names.
